subject: ConnX: next steps for private connectivity + SDK integration
messages:
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@connx.io>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, megan.li@connx.io
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + infra Qs from today

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful. A few quick infra and integration questions from our side so we can prep internal ops before the next call: 

1) Private connectivity: we heard two options on the call — VPC endpoint (PrivateLink-style) vs IP allowlist + egress. Which is recommended for tight regulatory controls? Any docs or expected IP ranges?

2) mTLS: does Redwood support mutual TLS for customer-to-service connections (client certs) or do you recommend TLS + API key? We need to know if client cert rotation is possible via our cert manager.

3) DNS & egress: how should we configure DNS for the model endpoints when using a private endpoint? Do we need to forward specific domains? Also, will embeddings generation call out to external storage (S3) from your infra or from our VPC?

4) SDK/auth: we plan to surface tool calling/structured-output in our product (invoice extraction + reranker). What auth patterns do you recommend for server-side SDK usage vs browser calls? Any advice on signing or short-lived creds?

If you can send a short checklist we can circulate with security. Attaching our internal network diagram and a one-pager of constraints.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a follow-up with infra folks.

—Sam
Infrastructure Lead, ConnX

Attachments: connx-network-questions.xlsx, connx-network-diagram.png

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + infra Qs from today

Sam — thanks for the note and the diagram, very helpful. High-level answers here; Diego will follow up with a technical checklist. I've flagged items we need to turn into action items below so your security team can review quickly.

Summary answers (short):
- For the tightest control and to avoid public IP allowlisting we recommend a private endpoint (Redwood Private: VPC endpoint + optional VPC peering or PrivateLink), but IP allowlisting + egress is a valid alternative when a private endpoint isn't possible.
- mTLS is supported for Private deployments — we support client certs with automated rotation via ACME or customer-managed PKI (your cert manager can provision). For Hosted, we recommend short-lived tokens + TLS (no client certs).
- DNS: when using a private endpoint you will configure a private hosted zone and either forward the model API domain(s) to Redwood’s VPC resolver or create a CNAME to the private endpoint. We'll share exact zone names.
- SDK/auth: server-side — short-lived JWTs (Redwood-issued) or per-service API keys; browser clients should always proxy through your backend to keep secrets off the client. We also support ephemeral client credentials for short-lived server-to-server flows.

Action items for ConnX security/infra (next steps):
1) Confirm whether you can accept a PrivateLink-style endpoint or need IP-allowlist only (reply: "PrivateEndpoint" or "IPAllowlist").
2) If PrivateEndpoint — provide the VPC ID, region, and preferred subnet for the endpoint (we'll return the private DNS names).
3) If IPAllowlist — confirm the egress NAT IPs (we'll provide Redwood's egress prefix list for your firewall).
4) Share your cert rotation preference (ACME vs managed PKI).
5) Identify a single eng contact for SDK auth integration (name + email).

I'll attach a short SOW draft and a one-page network checklist. Diego will reply with the low-level network checklist (ports, DNS FQDNs, cert parameters) by EOD tomorrow.

Would Tuesday 11/2 at 11:00 PT work for a 30-min follow-up with your network/security team?

Thanks — Priyom
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sow-draft.pdf

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: eng-team@connx.io, Megan Li <megan.li@connx.io>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@connx.io>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + infra Qs from today — technical checklist

Hi all — Diego from Redwood infra. Below is a concise technical checklist and guidance to share with your security/network team. I'll bring a copy to the call and we can walk through specifics.

A. Connectivity options (choose one):
- PrivateEndpoint (recommended for regulated workloads): we provision a PrivateLink endpoint in your account (or you create a VPC endpoint in your VPC that connects to Redwood’s PrivateLink). Requirements: provide VPC ID, subnet IDs for endpoint ENIs, and preferred AZs. We'll return private DNS FQDNs to resolve to endpoint IPs.
- IPAllowlist (fallback): we'll provide a stable egress prefix list. You must allow outbound HTTPS to those IP ranges on port 443 from your app servers. Note: IP allowlist exposes you to shared-hosted risk; recommended only if PrivateEndpoint is infeasible.

B. mTLS + certs:
- Private deployments: full mTLS supported. Redwood accepts x.509 client certs with RSA/ECDSA; we recommend ECDSA P-256.
- Cert TTLs: client certs can be short-lived (default 24h) or longer per your policy — we support automated rotation via ACME or manual upload to our PKI interface.
- Fields we check: CN = tenant-id, SAN = list of instance ids, and SHA256 fingerprint on upload. We'll provide an example CSR template.

C. DNS and egress behavior:
- DNS: Create a private hosted zone or conditional forwarder for the redwood-inference.internal domain we supply (e.g., api.private.redwood-inference.com). If using PrivateEndpoint we'll supply the private A records.
- Egress: Embeddings/rerank traffic initiated by your servers to the Redwood endpoint stays within your VPC -> Redwood PrivateLink. If you prefer our hosted flow (we host inference) and you use IPAllowlist, Redwood will make outbound calls to any configured external storage only if you supply signed credentials; otherwise, we recommend you proxy storage access.

D. SDK & auth patterns:
- Server-side recommended: use Redwood short-lived JWTs (example TTL 1h) issued via our token exchange endpoint. We support OAuth2 client credentials for long-running services.
- Browser clients: never embed secrets; route through your backend.
- Tool calling / structured output: use the SDK's function-calling mode. For sensitive outputs (PII extraction) configure response redaction and store outputs in your environment.

E. Embeddings & rerank guidance:
- Embeddings: recommend batching vectors in groups of 64–256 depending on vector size. Use async bulk endpoint for large inserts.
- Reranker: send candidate set as a single POST with document ids + short context; recommend K <= 50 for latency-sensitive flows, test with 16/32 as baseline.

F. Ports and FQDNs (example):
- Outbound: 443 to api.private.redwood-inference.com (PrivateEndpoint) or to Redwood egress ranges (we’ll send exact CIDRs).
- Mutual TLS port: 443 (standard).

Next steps we need from ConnX before the call:
1) Confirm chosen connectivity option (PrivateEndpoint or IPAllowlist).
2) If PrivateEndpoint: provide VPC ID, region, subnet IDs, and desired AZs.
3) If IPAllowlist: confirm firewall rules team and a point of contact for testing.
4) Confirm cert rotation approach (ACME vs. uploaded PKI certs).
5) Provide expected RPS and 95th percentile latency SLOs for reranking requests so we can size Dedicated slots if necessary.

I'll attach the checklist as a PDF on the call. See you at 11:00 PT.

—Diego
Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
